Subject: Priya Sharma — post-interview score reconciliation

Team — quick sync on Priya (final RN engineering loop). Attached two artifacts: the consolidated scorecard and my interview notes. Quick summary up front: technical bar = solid, system-design flagged as borderline for scale tradeoffs, culture / ownership score split among panelists (two 4s, one 2).

Can folks post your raw numeric scores in-thread (technical / design / ownership / hire) and flag any major blocking concerns? We're at the edge of an offer decision and need to close the loop by EOD Monday (PST). If you want to escalate for a tie-break, call it out and nominate someone who can weigh in.

Attachments: Priya_Sharma_scorecard.pdf, interview-notes-20261125.docx

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor

Neha / all — posting my scores below (raw):
- Technical: 5/5
- System design: 3/5 (solid fundamentals; unclear approach for high-concurrency caching at 100k qps)
- Ownership & async collaboration: 4/5
- Hire: Yes (strong IC + product sense)

Quick notes: Priya addressed follow-ups well but when pressed on multi-region failover she defaulted to higher-level abstractions (CDN/RDS) rather than a clear KV strategy. Not a blocker for IC4 but relevant for the team’s scale work.

If we need a tie-break between a 4 and a 3 for design, happy to talk it through — I can join a quick 15-min sync.

—Marissa

Posting my scores (raw):
- Technical: 4/5
- System design: 4/5 (liked the high-level cost/latency tradeoff framing; wanted slightly more on caching sharding)
- Ownership & async collaboration: 3/5 (good examples but fewer measurable outcomes called out)
- Hire: Yes, with reservation on ramp expectations

Rationale: I think the panel split on system design is more about depth vs. breadth. Marissa saw a gap in a specific high-concurrency pattern; I saw an acceptable approach that could be coached. If the team needs immediate senior-level system-design ownership, that could push us to pass; otherwise candidate is promotable.

If we need a tiebreak, I nominate Rishi (he's seen similar hires on infra) — Rishi, can you weigh in?

—Karthik

Thanks for the ping — saw notes and reviewed the recording. My read: solid engineering fundamentals and good product sense. On the specific design prompt (cache sharding + regional failover) she proposed a workable design but did not quantify failure modes or RTOs. Middle-of-the-road for system-design seniority.

My scores (raw):
- Technical: 4/5
- System design: 3/5
- Ownership: 4/5
- Hire: Yes (good long-term fit; recommend mentorship on design tradeoffs)

Given the panel: Marissa (5/3), Karthik (4/4), me (4/3) — I recommend we average and treat system design as 3.3 (rounded down to 3) for finalization, then pair Priya with a 6-week design onboarding plan if hired. I'll serve as the tie-breaker and back the hire contingent on the onboarding plan.

—Rishi

Awesome — thank you everyone for the quick turn. Finalized consensus: hire with development plan. Jordan will own the onboarding checkpoints; Rishi will be mentor partner for the first 6 weeks; Marissa / Karthik to add 1–2 coaching checkpoints below by EOD Tuesday.

Action items: 
- Jordan: draft 3 bullet onboarding success criteria for the offer packet and paste in this thread. (due Tue EOD PST)
- Neha (me): prep offer paperwork & attach success plan to the offer. (I will run comp with finance)
- Marissa / Karthik: add coaching checkpoints (e.g., quantify RTO/RPO examples; run one paired design review in week 3).
- Orchid Talent: please hold candidate while we send final offer; expect outreach tomorrow.

Links: candidate folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-priya-sharma), Greenhouse: GREENHOUSE-12345

Closing note to recruiter: please use \"hire contingent on 6-week onboarding plan\" language in the offer. Priya — we were impressed by your product intuition and would like to move forward; HR/recruiter will follow up with timing and comp details.

Thanks — Neha
